(Cedar Rapids, Iowa) * [[DME Academy]]
([[Daytona Beach, Florida]]) | college = [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] (2020–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 4 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–present | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2022|end}}) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * [[Karl Malone Award]] (2022) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2022) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|MOP]] ([[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2022]]) }} '''Keegan Mitchell Murray''' (born August 19, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]] before he was selected fourth overall by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He is the twin brother of [[Kris Murray]]. ==High school career== Murray played basketball for [[Prairie High School (Iowa)|Prairie High School]] in [[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]].{{cite web |last1=Goffin |first1=Isaac |title=Murray twins excited to compete together at college level |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2020/11/18/murray-twins-excited-to-compete-together-at-college-level/ |website=[[The Daily Iowan]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=November 18, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 20.3 points and 7.2 rebounds per game and was named Metro Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Prairie's Keegan Murray named all-Metro boys' basketball player of the year |url=https://www.thegazette.com/basketball/prairies-keegan-murray-named-all-metro-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=March 10, 2019}} Murray spent a [[postgraduate year]] at [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]] to gain more exposure.{{cite magazine |last1=Hensley |first1=Adam |title=Under The Radar: Keegan And Kris Murray's Journey To Iowa Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/murrays-recruit-041320 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=April 13, 2020}} He averaged 22.1 points and 7.5 rebounds per game, earning most outstanding player honors at the National Prep School Invitational.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Iowa commits Keegan and Kris Murray hit home run at DME Sports Academy |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/iowa-commits-keegan-and-kris-murray-hit-home-run-at-dme-sports-academy/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=April 1, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Keegan Murray |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/roster/keegan-murray/ |website=University of Iowa Athletics |date=17 June 2020 |access-date=May 24, 2021}} ==College career== [[File:Keegan Murray dunks vs Maryland at Xfinity Center in College Park MD, January 7th 2021 (Abdullah Konte - All Pro Reels Photography) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Murray dunking in January 2021]] As a three-star recruit, Murray committed to [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Keegan and Kris Murray commit to Iowa basketball, following in their dad's footsteps |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/keegan-and-kris-murray-commit-to-iowa-basketball-following-in-their-dads-footsteps/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=October 21, 2019}} On January 2, 2021, Murray recorded a freshman season-high 14 points, nine rebounds, three steals and three blocks in a 77–75 win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite web |last1=Hlas |first1=Mike |title=Keegan Murray gives Iowa men's basketball a lot of good things in win over Rutgers |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/keegan-murray-gives-iowa-mens-basketball-a-lot-of-good-things-in-win-over-rutgers/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=January 2, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.2 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game, earning [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=Keegan Murray, Patrick McCaffery will define next year's Iowa basketball season … and beyond |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2021/03/26/iowa-basketball-keegan-murray-patrick-mccaffery-future-stars-new-look-hawkeyes-2021-2022-season/6986297002/ |website=Hawk Central |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=March 26, 2021}} On November 16, 2021, Murray posted 27 points, 21 rebounds and four blocks in an 86–69 win against [[North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball|North Carolina Central]]. It was the first 20-point, 20-rebound game by an Iowa player since Bruce King in 1977.{{cite web |title=Murray Goes for 27/21 In Iowa Victory |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/news/2021/11/16/murray-goes-for-27-21-in-iowa-victory/ |website=University of Iowa Athletics |access-date=November 18, 2021 |date=November 16, 2021}} On November 29, he suffered an ankle injury during a 75–74 win over [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], forcing him to miss a game.{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Kennington |title=Iowa basketball star Keegan Murray to miss Purdue game due to ankle injury |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2021/12/03/iowa-basketball-keegan-murray-miss-purdue-game-due-ankle-injury-hawkeyes-big-ten-game/8861063002/ |access-date=December 3, 2021 |work=Hawk Central |date=December 3, 2021}} On December 18, Murray scored 35 points in a 94–75 victory over [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite news |title=Murray twins lead Iowa to 94-75 romp over Utah State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372127 |access-date=February 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 18, 2021}} He scored a career-high 37 points on February 13, 2022, in a 98–75 win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].{{cite news |title=Murray scores career-high 37 as Iowa pummels Nebraska 98-75 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364439 |access-date=February 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 13, 2022}} As a sophomore, Murray was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]],{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2022|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} and won the [[Karl Malone Award]] as the nation's top power forward.{{cite web|url=https://dailyiowan.com/2022/04/02/keegan-murray-wins-karl-malone-power-forward-of-the-year-award/ |title=Keegan Murray wins Karl Malone Power Forward of the Year Award |date=April 2, 2022 |access-date=April 5, 2022 |website=dailyiowan.com |language=en}} Additionally, he helped lead the Hawkeyes to a [[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] championship, being named [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player]]. On March 29, 2022, Murray declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2022 |title=Iowa All-American Murray is entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33624259/iowa-sophomore-basketball-player-keegan-murray-entering-nba-draft |access-date=March 29, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} == Professional career == === Sacramento Kings (2022–present) === In the [[2022 NBA draft]], Murray was selected with the fourth overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/nba-draft-2022-kings-pick-keegan-murray-no-4-over-jaden-ivey|title=Welcome to Sac: Kings draft Keegan Murray with No. 4 pick|website=NBC Sports|last=Thanawalla|first=Ali|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}} He made his [[2022 NBA Summer League|summer league]] debut on July 2 against the [[Golden State Warriors]], putting up 26 points and eight rebounds in an 86–68 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/kings-keegan-murray-scores-26-impressive-points-california-classic-debut|title=Kings' Murray stars in impressive California Classic debut|website=NBC Sports|last=Thanawalla|first=Ali|date=July 3, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}} Murray was named [[NBA Summer League]] MVP averaging 23 points, seven rebounds, two assists, one steal, while shooting 50% from the field and 40% from three-point range. He was also named to the All-NBA Summer League First Team.{{Cite web |title=Kings rookie Keegan Murray named MVP of NBA 2K23 Summer League |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kings-rookie-keegan-murray-named-mvp-of-nba-2k23-summer-league |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On October 22, Murray made his regular season debut, putting up 19 points, five rebounds, and two blocks in a 111–109 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-it-meant-everything-to-me-keegan-murray-message-to-kings-fans-after-standout-debut/|title='It meant everything to me': Keegan Murray's message to Kings fans after standout debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Samillano|first=Gerard|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} On January 20, 2023, Murray put up a then career-high 29 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in a 118–113 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/article271458652.html|title=Kings rookie Keegan Murray shows 'a little wiggle' in career night against Oklahoma City|website=The Sacramento Bee|last=Biderman|first=Chris|date=January 20, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2023}} On March 29, Murray made his 188th career three-pointer against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], surpassing [[Donovan Mitchell]]'s previous record (187) for the then record for most three-pointers made in a season by a rookie in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-keegan-murray-surpasses-donovan-mitchell-steph-curry-with-insane-rookie-3pt-feat|title=Kings forward Keegan Murray surpasses Donovan Mitchell, Steph Curry with insane rookie 3PT feat|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=March 29, 2023|access-date=March 29, 2023}} He finished his rookie season with 206 three-pointers.{{cite news |last1=Rodriguez |first1=Tristi |title=Why McNair believes Murray was NBA's most impactful rookie |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/kings-keegan-murray-was-nbas-most-impactful-rookie-monte-mcnair-declares |access-date=18 May 2023}} Murray was named to the 2023 [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{Cite news |last=Staff |first=John Hollinger and The Athletic |title=Banchero, Kessler among NBA All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4498687/2023/05/08/nba-all-rookie-team/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |work=The Athletic}} On December 16, 2023, Murray put up a career-high 47 points on 12-of-15 shooting from three-point range, including a league-record 11 made three-pointers in a row, in a 125–104 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |title=Kings' Murray drops 47, hits record 11 straight 3s |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39130316/keegan-murray-cans-record-11-straight-3s-47-point-performance |website=ESPN.com |access-date=18 December 2023 |language=en |date=17 December 2023}} He also became the youngest player in NBA history to make at least 12 three-pointers in a game at 23 years and 119 days old, surpassing the previous record set by [[Kobe Bryant]] at 24 years and 137 days old.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-stephen-curry-cant-believe-keegan-murray-12-triple-feat-in-kings-vs-jazz|title=Warriors' Stephen Curry can't believe Keegan Murray's 12-triple feat in Kings vs. Jazz|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=December 16, 2023|access-date=December 16, 2023}} On October 12, 2025, it was announced that Murray would miss at least 4-to-6 weeks due to a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] which required surgery.{{cite web | last=Rodriguez | first=Tristi | title=Doctor anticipates Kings forward Keegan Murray could miss at least three months with thumb injury | website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California | date=2025-10-14 | url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/sacramento-kings/keegan-murray-injury-recovery/1881386/?amp=1 | access-date=2025-12-07}} On October 16, Murray signed a five-year, $140 million contract extension with the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Keegan Murray to Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-keegan-murray-to-contract-extension|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2025|access-date=October 17, 2025}} He made 23 total appearances (including 22 starts) for Sacramento during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 14.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 1.7 assists. On May 13, 2026, Murray underwent [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] surgery to remove loose bodies from his left ankle.{{Cite web|title=Kings's Keegan Murray: Undergoes ankle surgery|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-keegan-murray-undergoes-ankle-surgery/|access-date=May 29, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
